sources.name: The Hacker News
sources.title: Linux KVM Flaw CVE-2026-99312 Lets Guest VMs Access Host Memory on AMD Hosts

stories.headline: Linux KVM flaw exposed 127 GB of host memory on AMD cloud servers
stories.dek: CVE-2026-99312 let a guest VM read a DigitalOcean host's RAM through nested virtualization; distribution kernels mostly remain unpatched.
stories.body:
A flaw in KVM, the hypervisor built into the Linux kernel, let researchers read about 127 GB of a DigitalOcean server's host memory from inside their own virtual machine, The Hacker News reports. On a shared server, that memory can include other customers' VMs. The bug, tracked as CVE-2026-99312, affects only hosts with AMD processors and nested virtualization enabled.

Oren Yomtov of Terra Security found the flaw and reported it through the provider's bug bounty program. The provider confirmed the exploit on its own hosts, treated it as critical and live-patched its fleet, telling Droplet customers that no action is needed. KVM maintainers, told on October 21, merged a fix on November 2. Fixed upstream kernels shipped Tuesday: stable 7.3.5 and long-term 6.18.64 and 6.12.118.

In a Droplet test, the host's kernel version banner came back first, followed by about 127 GB of host RAM mapped read-only. A separate write test on the researchers' own bare-metal AMD server placed 32 chosen bytes into a live host kernel page. Both tests required root inside a VM the attacker controls; network access alone is not enough. Terra traces the bug to a pointer left aimed at freed memory when an INIT reset stops a nested VM. Ironically, it was introduced by a 2022 fix for CVE-2022-3344 and sat in the kernel for nearly four years.

Severity ratings disagree. The kernel's CVE team scores it 8.8 out of 10. Red Hat's preliminary assessment rates it Moderate at 5.6, treating it as denial-of-service only. Ubuntu rates it High. According to VirtFusion, there are no reports of exploitation outside research, and no exploit code has been published.

Operators running their own AMD KVM hosts face the harder job. Debian lists all releases as vulnerable outside unstable, Ubuntu has no fixed package yet, and Red Hat lists Enterprise Linux 9 and 10 as affected with the fix deferred. Nested virtualization is on by default in the kvm_amd module, per VirtFusion. Until a patched host kernel is installed and the host rebooted, the only protection is setting kvm_amd nested=0, which stops tenants from running VMs inside their VMs. Intel hosts are not affected.
key_points: CVE-2026-99312 hits AMD KVM hosts with nested virtualization enabled
Researchers read about 127 GB of a DigitalOcean host's RAM
Fixed in kernels 7.3.5, 6.18.64 and 6.12.118; most distros unpatched
Severity scores range from 5.6 (Red Hat) to 8.8 (kernel CVE team)
stories.why_it_matters: Anyone running AMD KVM hosts should check /sys/module/kvm_amd/parameters/nested and patch or disable it, since updating guest OSes does nothing. Cloud tenants on providers like DigitalOcean are already covered.

sources.name: PostgreSQL Global Development Group
sources.title: PostgreSQL 19 released with concurrent REPACK and planner advice

stories.headline: PostgreSQL 19 ships REPACK CONCURRENTLY and planner advice
stories.dek: The new major release reclaims table space without blocking traffic, lets developers steer the planner and turns JIT off by default.
stories.body:
The PostgreSQL Global Development Group released PostgreSQL 19 on November 19. The headline feature is a new REPACK command that reclaims disk space and reorganizes table contents. Run as REPACK (CONCURRENTLY), it does this without blocking reads or writes to the table, according to the release notes. A new system view, pg_stat_progress_repack, reports progress for REPACK, CLUSTER and VACUUM FULL.

The second big addition targets query plans. The pg_plan_advice extension lets developers control query planner decisions, and a companion extension, pg_stash_advice, applies that advice automatically based on the query. Planner work goes further: NOT IN clauses can become more efficient anti joins when NULLs are absent, some aggregation can happen before joins, and foreign-key checks are faster.

Replication gets several upgrades. Logical replication can now be enabled without a server restart when wal_level is set to replica. Sequence values can be replicated logically. A new WAIT command supports read-your-writes consistency on standbys, so an application can read back its own writes from a replica. Autovacuum can now process table indexes in parallel and uses a new scoring system to decide which tables to handle first.

There are also quieter performance changes. The number of I/O worker processes now scales automatically, replacing the io_workers setting with four new variables. COPY FROM uses SIMD instructions for text and CSV input, sorting uses radix sort, and the default TOAST compression moves from pglz to lz4. NOTIFY now only wakes backends that are listening.

Upgraders should read the compatibility list carefully. JIT is now disabled by default because its cost-based activation proved unreliable, so sites running many large analytical queries must turn it back on. The default max_locks_per_transaction rises from 64 to 128, but lock allocation changed, so existing settings must effectively be doubled. RADIUS support is gone, standard_conforming_strings is always on, MD5 password logins trigger a warning, and the MULE_INTERNAL encoding is removed. Parallel vacuum may run slower because workers now share one cost limit.

Moving data from any earlier release requires pg_dumpall, pg_upgrade or logical replication. The project recommends reindexing full text search and pg_trgm indexes after pg_upgrade in some locale setups.
key_points: REPACK (CONCURRENTLY) reclaims space without blocking reads or writes
pg_plan_advice and pg_stash_advice let users steer the planner
Logical replication enabled without restart; sequences now replicate
JIT now off by default; max_locks_per_transaction default doubles to 128
stories.why_it_matters: Bloated tables can now be compacted in production without downtime, and replicas can guarantee read-your-writes. Check JIT, lock settings and old dumps before upgrading.

sources.name: Hacker News
sources.title: Levent Alpöge claims proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis [pdf]

stories.headline: Mathematician Levent Alpöge claims proof of Generalized Riemann Hypothesis
stories.dek: The unverified claim, posted as a PDF, drew nearly 2,500 points and over 1,700 comments on Hacker News.
stories.body:
Mathematician Levent Alpöge has posted a PDF claiming a proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis. The claim has not been verified, and no independent review has been reported. The document appeared on his website, alpo.ge, and was shared on Hacker News on November 20, where it reached 2,496 points and 1,719 comments.

The Generalized Riemann Hypothesis extends the original Riemann Hypothesis, one of the best-known open problems in mathematics, to a broader family of functions. Many results in number theory are proven on the assumption that it holds.

Claimed proofs of major conjectures are common, and most do not survive scrutiny. Any confirmation would depend on detailed checking by specialists, which typically takes months or longer.
key_points: Levent Alpöge has posted a PDF claiming a proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis.
The claim is unverified and awaits review by other mathematicians.
The Hacker News post drew 2,496 points and 1,719 comments.

sources.name: BleepingComputer
sources.title: Hackers use autonomous AI tool Cairn to find zero-day, take over server

stories.headline: Hackers turn AI pentest tool Cairn on medical imaging app, root server
stories.dek: Amazon says suspected Chinese-linked attackers told AI agents to "obtain shell access" and they found a zero-day in MONAI Label.
stories.body:
Suspected Chinese-linked hackers used Cairn, an open-source autonomous AI pentesting framework, to find a zero-day in the MONAI Label medical imaging application and take full control of a server, BleepingComputer reports, citing Amazon Threat Intelligence. The attackers instructed the agents to "obtain shell access" and left them to find and exploit a path traversal flaw on their own. The agents went from mapping the API to exploitation in 11 minutes, then wrote a Python reverse shell into sitecustomize.py to gain root.

Amazon found the campaign, which ran September 8 to 10 and mainly hit East Asian universities, because the attackers left their Cairn instance exposed without authentication. The agents also failed at times, including a 16-hour attempt on a Redis server. MONAI Label maintainers shipped a fix on November 18.
key_points: Amazon attributes the campaign to a Chinese-nexus actor with moderate confidence; it ran September 8 to 10, 2026.
Cairn's agents exploited a MONAI Label path traversal zero-day within 11 minutes of mapping its API.
MONAI Label maintainers released a security update on November 18.

sources.name: TechRadar
sources.title: Anthropic mathematician says Claude helped him solve a 167-year-old math problem

stories.headline: Anthropic mathematician claims Claude helped prove Riemann hypothesis
stories.dek: Levent Alpöge's proof exists only in Lean and still needs independent vetting before any $1 million Millennium Prize payout.
stories.body:
Anthropic number theorist Levent Alpöge says he has proved the Riemann hypothesis, the 167-year-old problem about the distribution of prime numbers, with help from Claude, TechRadar reports. In a statement on his personal website, Alpöge wrote that the method also resolves the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis. He said Claude "far outpaced me near the finish line."

The proof is not yet independently verified. It exists only in the Lean proof language, with no human-readable version. According to TechRadar, an early draft ran past 250,000 pages. The Riemann hypothesis is one of the Millennium Prize problems, which carry a $1 million award, but the rules require two years of scrutiny before any payout.

The claim lands right after Anthropic's $1.7 trillion stock market debut. Alpöge called the timing "horrible" but said the cynical view "is false."
key_points: Levent Alpöge of Anthropic claims a Claude-assisted proof of the Riemann hypothesis, per TechRadar.
The proof is written only in Lean and has not been independently verified.
A Millennium Prize of $1 million is possible only after two years of scrutiny.

sources.name: Signal
sources.title: Signal blocks Siri and Gemini AI assistants from reading chats

stories.headline: Signal blocks Siri and Gemini from reading chats on phones
stories.dek: The app now blocks screenshots on iOS 27 and turns on screen security when Android assistants try to read the screen, but macOS stays unprotected.
stories.body:
Signal is blocking OS-level AI assistants from capturing chats on iOS 27 and Android, the nonprofit said in a blog post. On iOS 27 the app now prevents screenshots. On Android it automatically turns on its "Screen security" setting when it detects an assistant trying to read the screen. Users can switch the protection off in settings, though Signal warns that this exposes their contacts' messages too.

The move extends last year's default screenshot block against Microsoft's Recall on Windows 11. Signal calls agentic features like Gemini Intelligence and Siri's Onscreen Awareness an "existential threat" to app-level privacy. It cannot block Siri on macOS, citing a lack of documented APIs, and admits the fix misses other routes such as filesystem access. Signal is asking Apple, Google and Microsoft for a simple opt-out and better documentation.
key_points: Signal blocks screenshots on iOS 27 and enables screen security on Android when an AI assistant tries to read the screen.
Protection can be disabled in settings; macOS is not covered, and Signal suggests excluding the app in Siri settings.
Signal wants Apple, Google and Microsoft to offer a documented AI opt-out for developers.

sources.name: MISSIL
sources.title: GTA VI har sålts i 32,5 miljoner exemplar på 24 timmar

stories.headline: GTA VI earns $3.79 billion on launch day, Rockstar says
stories.dek: Take-Two cites 32.5 million copies, though PC Gamer and Sweden's MISSIL describe that figure differently: preorders versus first-day sales.
stories.body:
Grand Theft Auto VI pulled in $3.79 billion in "day one retail sales," Rockstar Games says, calling it "the biggest entertainment launch in history." PC Gamer notes that a single day beats the entire theatrical run of Avengers: Endgame, which earned a little more than $2.9 billion.

The copy count is less clear-cut. PC Gamer reports that Take-Two said the game sold 32.5 million copies in pre-release, "a new record across all platforms." Swedish outlet MISSIL instead reports 32.5 million copies sold in 24 hours.

According to PC Gamer, the one-day haul tops Take-Two's net revenue guidance for the whole quarter by nearly $400 million at the high end. Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick had earlier called preorder levels "unprecedented" without giving numbers. For scale, GTA V sold a little over 11 million copies on launch day in 2013 and has since passed 230 million.
key_points: Rockstar reports $3.79 billion in day-one retail sales for GTA VI.
PC Gamer describes 32.5 million copies as pre-release sales; MISSIL reports them as sold in 24 hours.
The launch-day total exceeds Take-Two's quarterly revenue guidance by nearly $400 million at the high end, per PC Gamer.

sources.name: The Hacker News
sources.title: Hackers Exploit Critical Cisco Expressway Flaw, Breach Four Devices and Reach Internal Network

stories.headline: Attackers exploit critical Cisco Expressway flaw after public PoC
stories.dek: Russian security firm F6 says intruders gained root on four Expressway devices at one organization and moved into its internal network.
stories.body:
Attackers exploited a critical Cisco Expressway vulnerability shortly after a proof-of-concept exploit went public, breaching four devices at a Russian organization, The Hacker News reports. The flaw, CVE-2026-76466, carries a CVSS score of 9.8 and lets an unauthenticated remote attacker run operating system commands as root. Cisco patched it on October 21, 2026, in release X15.5.20.

Russian security company F6 says the attackers first compromised two internet-facing Expressway X15.5.3 devices, then used one to reach two cluster nodes on the internal network. From there, they used custom Python scripts to scan the network, probe SMB, SQL Server, WinRM and GitLab, and exfiltrate credentials. F6 says the scripts were possibly written with AI help.

The attack has not been attributed to any known group. Admins should update and check for compromise.
key_points: CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS 9.8) allows unauthenticated root command execution on Cisco Expressway; fixed in X15.5.20 on October 21, 2026.
F6 says attackers breached two internet-facing devices and two internal cluster nodes, then moved laterally to steal credentials.
Indicators include "wombat@127.0.0.1" in erlang.log and Python scripts staged under /mnt/harddisk.
